briefing.topLine: Former NSW opposition leader Mark Speakman has announced his resignation, with The Guardian reporting he warned in a late-night speech that the Liberals face an "existential threat" — the Daily Telegraph describes him as the seventh Liberal MP to quit under leader Kellie Sloane. Labor meanwhile unveiled Parramatta councillor and former Liberal staffer Tanya Raffoul as its candidate for the marginal seat of Epping, a recruitment the ABC reports as unprecedented. Locally, the Illawarra Mercury sets out a $621 million state budget plan aimed at ending rain-related shutdowns on the South Coast rail line.
briefing.localWatch: The South Coast line's Coalcliff rain-gauge shutdowns are the target of a $621m state spend, while Nowra gains 75 maintenance jobs with new Seahawk helicopters at HMAS Albatross. Kiama Council is weighing organisational reforms alongside its special rate variation consultation, and Shoalhaven planning fights continue over a 77-unit Huskisson proposal and a stalled Nowra helicopter display.

stories.headline: What's at Coalcliff that can shut down the South Coast rail line?
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that a rain gauge at Coalcliff triggers a halt to South Coast trains at 100mm, and explains how a $621 million NSW budget commitment is intended to lift those limits and reduce regular commuter shutdowns.

stories.headline: New Navy helicopters arrive to help jobs boom that is transforming Nowra
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports HMAS Albatross has taken delivery of two new Seahawk helicopters, which it says will deliver 75 maintenance jobs in Nowra. The paper examines what the region's defence expansion means for local housing.

stories.headline: Helicopter on a stick still grounded as governments argue about location
stories.summary: The South Coast Register reports Defence Minister Richard Marles has urged Shoalhaven City Council to approve a replica Seahawk Romeo display for Nowra. According to the outlet, plans remain stalled amid claims about safety and a land dispute.

stories.headline: Council to consider organisational reforms along with SRV consultation
stories.summary: Kiama Council says it will consider organisational reforms alongside consultation on a special rate variation.

stories.headline: Coastal development information event rated as "highly beneficial" by organisers
stories.summary: The Milton Ulladulla Times reports Shoalhaven City Council has received more than 350 objections to a proposed 77-apartment development at Huskisson, and sets out why residents and visitors are opposing the plan.

stories.headline: 'Behave yourself': The F-word sparks a reaction from Kiama Mayor Cameron McDonald
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Kiama Mayor Cameron McDonald apologised to Councillor Matt Brown after mishearing him during a debate on planning notices, in what the paper describes as a heated chamber exchange.

stories.headline: Former NSW Opposition Leader Mark Speakman announces shock resignation
stories.summary: Mark Speakman has announced his resignation, with the Daily Telegraph describing him as the seventh NSW Liberal MP to resign under leader Kellie Sloane. The Guardian reports that in a late-night speech the former opposition leader said the party faces an "existential threat" and warned against it becoming "Labor lite" or "One Nation lite".

stories.headline: 'This has never happened before': Minns picks former Liberal
stories.summary: Premier Chris Minns has announced Parramatta councillor Tanya Raffoul, a former staffer to Coalition police minister David Elliott, as Labor's candidate for the marginal seat of Epping. The ABC reports she was recruited by her former political rivals after quitting the Liberals; the Daily Telegraph describes the move as a defection and a Labor coup.

stories.headline: One Nation in turmoil as under-fire party manager goes on leave
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports One Nation's general manager has gone on leave, weeks after the masthead reported allegations that the manager downplayed the rape conviction of a senior party official. The allegations are as reported by the masthead and have not been tested.

stories.headline: ‘We should be adding homes, not losing them’: Sydney’s shrinking housing supply
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports that older, more affordable unit blocks in Sydney's east are being demolished and replaced with fewer, larger apartments, raising questions about net housing supply.

stories.headline: Minns in the doghouse over broken animal protection promises
stories.summary: The Daily Telegraph reports the Minns government has been accused of weakening an independent animal welfare body and failing to deliver on animal protection commitments. The claims are as reported by the outlet.

stories.headline: GTA VI release puts NSW's lacklustre game development funding in spotlight
stories.summary: The ABC reports Screen NSW offers up to $30,000 per video game in state funding, and that developers say this is insufficient, with some leaving the state for better offers elsewhere.

stories.headline: Tammy Shipley was supposed to be monitored in prison. Instead she died after drinking 20L of water
stories.summary: A coroner has found the death of Aboriginal woman Tammy Michelle Shipley, 47, at Silverwater women's correctional centre in December 2022 was preventable and resulted from systemic failures, The Guardian reports. According to the findings as reported, her excess water consumption would have been prevented had she been checked at the required intervals.

stories.headline: Progress on caseworker vacancy rates after minister's ex-gratia grilling
stories.summary: The Newcastle Herald reports NSW Minister Kate Washington has faced scrutiny over her approval of a $15,000 ex-gratia payment to a foster carer, including concerns raised within her department, alongside discussion of caseworker vacancy rates.

stories.headline: Residents in Bunnings towers will be trapped during flood: council
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Wollongong City Council has raised a series of concerns about a proposed tower development, including that residents could be trapped during a flood.

stories.headline: Concerns over 330m wall that will block access to Lake Illawarra entrance channel
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports community concern over a planned rock wall at the Lake Illawarra entrance channel, with the council describing the "emergency" work as a short-term measure.

stories.headline: The realignment reaches Epping
stories.summary: Ben Raue examines Labor's announcement that Tanya Raffoul, the City of Parramatta councillor for Dundas ward, will contest Epping, placing the preselection in the context of a broader political realignment.

stories.headline: Architect of party triumphs says Victorian Labor has ‘had good run’
stories.summary: The Australian Financial Review reports the view of a key architect of past Labor state campaigns that the Victorian contest is effectively decided, while arguing there is still time for Chris Minns in NSW.

stories.headline: 'Double-edged sword': House price rebound for Sydney after market downturn
stories.summary: New property analysis cited by the ABC forecasts Sydney leading the recovery from the national housing market slump.

stories.headline: One Nation candidate's migrant welfare graph completely wrong, researcher says
stories.summary: The ABC reports that One Nation candidate Katherine Deves used a graph of Australian welfare rates by country of birth to argue for deep cuts to migration, and that a leading researcher says the graph is "completely wrong".

elsewhere.text: Federally, The Conversation reports the Coalition has taken the primary vote lead in a Morgan poll, while a YouGov poll has Labor at an equal record low and the Greens at an equal record high.
